summary: Provisioning agent crashloop after NVMe secure-erase during depot repair
description:
Issue summary: Devices returned from depot repair with NVMe secure-erase performed are entering a provisioning agent crashloop during OOBE task sequence. Impact: New hire devices cannot complete autopilot/enrollment, blocking onboarding for a small cohort. Scope: Observed in 6 devices from same repair batch.

Impact: Users cannot finish device setup; devices repeatedly reboot into provisioning agent restart loop and fail to register in Intune/AzureAD. Time sensitive because these are scheduled new-hire machines.

Environment: Staged Windows 11 Corp image, corporate OOBE/autopilot flow, repair vendor performed NVMe secure-erase with vendor utility prior to returning hardware.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Receive depot-repaired device where NVMe was secure-erased using vendor tool.
2) Boot device to image USB and apply corporate Windows 11 image (autopilot-aware).
3) Reboot into OOBE/autopilot flow.
4) Provisioning agent (CompanyProvisionAgent v3.8.1) starts and crashes repeatedly after initializing TPM and reading NVMe SMART.
5) Device reboots and repeats.
observed_behavior: Provisioning agent exits with non-zero code and crashloop restarts. Device never reaches Intune enroll/prompt for corporate account. Event Viewer shows repeated Service Control Manager restarts for CompanyProvisionAgent service. Imaging logs show NVMe device node re-initialized with transient SMART/WWN mismatch warnings.
expected_behavior: Device should complete OOBE/autopilot provisioning, register to Intune/AzureAD, and apply corp policies. Provisioning agent should handle NVMe secure-erase state gracefully.
logs:
EventLog snippet:
- Application: CompanyProvisionAgent.exe faulting module nvme_adapter.dll, ExceptionCode: 0xc0000005.
- System: Disk 0 re-enumerated: New Namespace GUID mismatch (expected WWN a1b2c3..., saw 000000...).
- Provisioning log (C:\ProgramData\Company\Provision\provision.log): 'ERR nvme: namespace-metadata invalid; aborting init'
- Repair vendor ticket: RMA-77821: 'Performed NVMe secure-erase to NIST-compliant purge.'
investigation_notes:
Hypothesis 1: Secure-erase removes vendor metadata/WWN mapping the provisioning agent expects. Agent code does not handle empty or zeroed NVMe namespace metadata and dereferences null leading to access violation.
Hypothesis 2: TPM NVMe binding used by agent to verify drive identity fails after secure-erase; agent hits an unexpected code path and crashes.
Findings: Reproduced on 2 devices in lab using vendor secure-erase utility. Replacing nvme_adapter.dll with debug build shows null pointer deref when reading SMART vendor fields. Booting without secure-erase (standard sanitize) does not reproduce.
Related traces: Added kernel log capture and live debug via WinDbg; callstack indicates crash in nvme_adapter!ParseNamespaceMetadata -> CompanyProvisionAgent!InitStorageBindings.
Potential risk: If fleet repair vendors use secure-erase, similar failures will occur at scale.
Mitigation options considered: Add defensive checks in agent to tolerate missing metadata; update repair SOP to use sanitize instead of secure-erase; vendor-side preserve NVMe metadata when possible.
comments: 2026-03-10 | Miguel Ortega (Support): Affected devices came from vendor depot batch RMA-77821. Sent initial triage logs to SRE. Marked as P1 due to onboarding impact.
2026-03-10 | Riley Park (SRE): Confirmed crashloop on two lab reproductions. Collecting WinDbg dumps and nvme metadata dumps. Assigned to provisioning team for code fix or defensive patch.

2026-03-11 | Emily Chen (Repair Ops): Reached out to vendor; vendor confirms they run secure-erase for compliance. Asked vendor to pause secure-erase on next batch and provide hardware log. Vendor asked for remediation recommendation.
2026-03-11 | Dev (Provisioning) - PR link: https://github.com/redwood/provisioning-agent/pull/412 - adding defensive checks and fallback path to skip NVMe metadata binding when not present.

2026-03-12 | Riley Park (SRE): Temporary workaround validated: install 'agent-hotfix-2026-03' which catches null metadata and continues enrollment. Workaround applied to 6 devices manually and they completed enrollment.
resolution:
Workaround: Applied agent-hotfix-2026-03 to affected devices to bypass strict NVMe metadata binding. Recommended immediate operational change: Repair Ops to instruct vendor to use 'sanitize' instead of 'secure-erase' until agent patch is rolled out fleet-wide.
Long-term fix: Provisioning team to merge PR#412 which adds defensive handling for missing NVMe metadata and a feature flag to enable permissive storage binding; scheduled rollout to staging on 2026-03-15 and prod on 2026-03-22 after verification.
Post-action: Created runbook 'NVMe-SecureErase-Handling' and vendor bulletin. Notify Onboarding squad about potential delayed enrollments for affected serial ranges.
